sentences.text:
This suit is instituted by the plaintiffs against the defendant for the relief of permanent injunction,
restraining the defendant, his agents, workers, legal representatives or anybody claiming under him from interfering with plaintiffs possession and enjoyment of suit property and pass such other reliefs.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:
Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
2
That, suit schedule property was sold by Binny Mill Housing Co-operative Society under registered sale deed dated 03.12.1982 in favour of husband of plaintiff namely Nanjaiah.
Husband of original plaintiff during his lifetime executed Will dated 01.12.2008 bequeathing suit property in favour of plaintiff.
Husband of plaintiff died on 09.12.2008.
By virtue of Will executed by her husband, original plaintiff become absolute owner and in possession and enjoyment of suit property.

On 02.12.2022,
plaintiff attempted to start construction of compound Wall to suit property, all of sudden defendant appeared and started to interfere in plaintiffs possession and enjoyment of suit property by contending he has filed suit in O.S.No.4334/2021 against Sri Deva Kumar, Rajesh and Mahadev.
Plaintiff is not party to O.S.No.4334/2021.
Defendant is stranger to plaintiff and suit property.
The defendant allegedly being care taker of one Narayanaswamy is claiming illegal right over alleged land left behind by Narayanaswamy.
The defendant is making hectic efforts to grab suit property by illegal way.
There is no agricultural land near suit property.

The defendant who is not in physical possession or who having no right,
title and interest is attempting to take physical possession of suit property.
On these pleadings, the plaintiffs have prayed to decree suit as prayed in plaint.
3. In response to the service of suit summons, defendant has tendered his appearance before the court through his counsel and contested the case.

4. The contents of written statement of defendant in brief are as under :-
That, suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same liable to be dismissed.
It is contended that, plaintiff having full knowledge that, suit property is in possession of defendant.
Plaintiff is not in possession of suit property.
Defendant is in possession of entire Sy.No.8, measuring 1 acre 16 guntas out of which 3 guntas phot kharab land.
Suit filed by plaintiffs for bare injunction is not maintainable.
There is heavy cloud casted over title of suit property.

Originally Sy.No.8 measuring 1 acre 16 guntas belonging to one Narayanappa S/o.
Venkatakrishnan.
Defendant was working with said Narayanappa in his Farm house constructed in Sy.No.8.
Narayanappa was cultivating said land by using Vrushabhavathi River Water and he was doing Horticulture and Animal husbandry with help of defendant.

Narayanappa settled in abroad in the year 1980 by executing letter of relinquishment of right and title dated 06.08.1980 in said property in the name of defendant and handed over physical possession of entire land bearing Sy.No.8 to defendant.
Thereafter, defendant has been continued in possession of entire Sy.No.8 including suit schedule property.

The defendant to the knowledge of true owner has continued in possession of above mentioned property for more than 40 years, hence he become absolute owner of suit property by virtue of adverse possession.
The defendant is residing in suit property and also running animal husbandry business.
Smt. Rajamma and her daughter Smt. Chandrakala have filed suit for partition in O.S.No.4826/2007 in which Sy.No.8 also included.
The defendant sought impleading in said suit and ultimately it was dismissed.

The Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
3 plaintiff filed suit in O.S.No.9474/2007 against Smt. Rajamma and others.
Said suit was decreed by holding defendant is in possession of suit property.

On these grounds,
it is requested to dismiss the suit.

5. On the basis of above pleadings of both parties, this court has framed the following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether plaintiff proves that, as on date of filing suit he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property?
2. Whether plaintiff further proves that, alleged interference by the defendant in her lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property?
3. Whether defendant proves that, suit filed by plaintiff in present form for bare injunction is not at all maintainable?
4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief as prayed?
5. What order or decree?
6. To substantiate the case of the plaintiffs, the General Power of Attorney of plaintiff examined himself as PW1 and produced in all 59 documents as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.59.

On the other hand, the defendant examined himself as D.W.1 and produced 54 documents as Exs.D.1 to D.54.
7.
I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for plaintiff and learned counsel for defendants and I have perused the case records.
ISSUE No.1 AND 2 :- As these issues are inter- related to each other and involves common appreciation of facts and evidence on record, findings on one issue are bearing on other issue
, in order to avoid repetition of facts and for convenience sake, both issues are taken together for common discussion.

10. The original plaintiff has claimed her title and possession over suit schedule mentioned property based on registered Will dated 01.12.2008 said to have been executed by her husband Sri Nanjaiah in respect of suit property in her favour.

After death of original plaintiff, her legal representatives,
who are plaintiffs herein are claiming their right and possession over suit property being children of late Sri Nanjaiah and Smt. Nanjamma.
On the other hand, it is specific case of defendant that, entire Sy.No.8, situated at Divatige Ramanahalli, measuring 1 acre 16 guntas originally belonged to Narayanappa.

During 1980, said Narayanappa left Bengaluru and joined his children, who are in abroad and executed letter of relinquishment of right and title in respect of entire Sy.No.8 in favour of defendant herein.
It is the defendant since more than 40 years has continued in possession and enjoyment of entire extent of Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village.
It is specific contention of defendant that, plaintiffs are not in possession and enjoyment of suit property.

11. It is pleaded in the plaint and same is deposed by plaintiff No.1(c) who examined P.W.1 that, on 03.12.1982 Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society has sold suit property in favour of Sri Nanjaiah under registered sale deed and on 22.02.1983 possession certificate was issued.

Thereafter,
Nanjaiah who is father of present plaintiffs continued in possession and enjoyment of suit property.
12. The plaintiffs in order to show, Binni Mills Workers and other labors Co-operative Housing Society has sold suit property in favour of late Nanjaiah S/o.
Kempaiah has produced sale deed as per Ex.P.7.
On careful perusal of said document, it is mentioned site No.50 in Sy.No.8 at Divatige Ramanahalli Village, which is in K.H.Raganatha Colony sold to Nanjaiah by society.
Ex.P.8 is possession certificate dated 22.02.1983 in respect of suit property in favour of Nanjaiah.
The plaintiffs have also produced share certificate issued by Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society in the name of Nanjaiah.
13. The plaintiffs have produced encumbrance certificate as per Ex.P.12 in respect of suit property.
In said document, it is clearly mentioned about sale deed dated 03.12.1982 executed by Binni Mills Housing Co- operative society in favour of Nanjaiah.

entities.text: Binni Mills Housing Co- operative society
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P.14 to P.27 are tax paid receipts pertaining to suit property from the year 2014 to 2021 issued in the name of original plaintiff- Smt. Nanjamma.
14. It is pertinent to note here that, schedule property shown in sale deed as per Ex.P.7 and schedule of suit property shown in schedule to the plaintiff are one and the same.

The defendant in order to show, Sy.No.8 measuring 1 acre 16 guntas is agricultural land and same is still standing the name of Narayanappa has produced records of rights for the year 2007 as per Ex.D.3.
15.
On perusal of Ex.D.3, it is mentioned the names of Narayanappa and Venkatakrishnan as owner and possessor of said property.
The defendant has further produced survey sketch and Akharaband in respect of Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village as per Ex.D.4 and D.5 wherein an extent of property shown as 1 acre 16 guntas.

Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
5 16.
The P.W.1 in his cross-examination has deposed, he has not produced any documents to show,
Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society has acquired title overs Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village.
It is deposed by P.W.1 that, it may be true, Sy.No.8 measuring 1 acre 16 guntas of Divatige Ramanahalli Village originally belonged to Narayanappa S/o. Venkatakrishna.
It is suggested to P.W.1 that, sale deed relied by plaintiffs is created document, same is denied as false.
17. The D.W.1 in his cross-examination has deposed, Sy.No.8 to an extent of 1 acre 16 guntas belonged to Narayanappa.
It is further say of D.W.1 that, he was working under said Narayanappa.
Sons of Narayanappa settled in abroad.
In the year 1980, Narayanappa joined his sons, who are in abroad and executed relinquishment deed in respect of Sy.No.8 in favour of defendant.

As such,
since 40 years, he is in possession and enjoyment of entire extent of Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village.
18. The D.W.1 in his cross-examination has further deposed, relinquishment deed executed by Narayanappa is not registered one.
It is say of D.W.1 that, he knows about Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society formed layout in Sy.No.8.
It is specifically stated that, as there exists Rushabhavathi River said property was left out while forming layout.

19. In view of evidence of D.W.1 as referred supra, he is indirectly admitting Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village was acquired for formation of layout by Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society.
It is only contention of D.W.1 that, as there exists Rushabhavathi River, Sy.No.8 was left out in formation layout.
In further cross-examination of D.W.1 has deposed, Sy.No.8 to an extent of 1 acre 16 guntas not involved in acquisition proceedings.
20. It is worth to note here that, Ex.P.7 is registered sale deed executed by Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society in respect of suit property in favour of Nanjaiah at undisputed point of time.
Registration of sale deed reinforces valid execution of sale deed and carries presumption of validity.
Burden of proof lies on party challenging validity.

In this regard, the learned counsel for plaintiffs has relied upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in AIR 209 SC 72 in case of Jamila Begum (Dead) by LR's Vs. Shami Mohammed (d) by LR's wherein it is held that, a registered document carries with it a presumption that it was validly executed.

entities.text: Jamila Begum (Dead) by LR's Vs. Shami Mohammed (d)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is for the other party challenging genuineness of transaction to show transaction is not valid in law.
There is presumption that, registered document is validly executed.
A registered document therefore, prima facie would be valid in law.

21. It is worth to note here that, as already discussed, sale deed as per Ex.P.7 and possession certificate as per Ex.P.8 were executed by Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society in favour of Nanjaiah in respect of suit property at undisputed point of time.

Further, at no point of time, those deeds have been challenged by executant Binni Mills Housing Co- operative Society or by Narayanappa, who is original owner of Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village.

entities.text: Binni Mills Housing Co- operative Society
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per recital of Exs.P.7 and P.8 possession of suit property as described in schedule to plaint was handed over by society to Nanjaiah.

Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
6 22.

The claim of possession over entire extent of Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village by defendant is mainly based on judgment and orders in earlier proceedings as well as complaint and photos produced before the court as per Exs.D.6 to D.38.

It is worth to note here that, defendant has produced certified copy of plaint in O.S.No.4826/2007 as per Ex.D.8.
23.

It is specifically contended and it is evident from Ex.D.8 that, Smt. Rajamma and Smt.
Chandrappa claiming to be legal heirs of Narayanappa have filed suit for partition against other legal heirs of Narayanappa wherein Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village also included.

It is specifically contented and same is deposed by D.W.1 that, in said suit, defendant filed application to implead him as party because property in his possession bearing Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village was included.
An application filed by defendant was dismissed.
Hence, defendant filed suit in O.S.No.9474/2007 against Smt. Rajamma and others.

Certified copy of judgment in O.S.No.9474/2007 has been produced as per Ex.D.35.
24.

It is evident from Ex.D.35 that, suit filed by defendant herein against Smt. Rajamma and others partly decreed and it was held, defendant herein is in possession of 1 acre 16 gunts in Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village.

25. Further, defendant has produced Ex.D.37 and D.38 which are certified copies of orders in Misc.
Petition No.209/2010 to show Smt. Rajamma and others have violated injunction order passed by court and after enquiry, petition filed by defendant was allowed and respondent therein are directed by the court to pay compensation to defendant herein.
26.
The defendant has further produced certified copy of complaint, photos, FIR and order sheet Proceedings in criminal case, letter addressed to Hon'ble Governor of Karnataka as per Exs.D.10 to D.32.
Photos have been produced as per Ex.D.39 to D.53 and CD produced as per Ex.D.54.

The D.W.1 in his cross- examination has denied suggestion put forth by learned counsel for plaintiff that,
he has created Exs.D.3 to D.54 for the purpose of present suit.

27. It is worth to note here that, no doubt in earlier proceedings as relied by defendant, courts have held that defendant is in possession of Sy.No.8 measuring 1 acre 16 guntas situated at Divatige Ramanahalli Village but either original plaintiff or present plaintiffs are not parties to those proceedings.
The D.W.1 in his cross-examination
has deposed, Sy.No.8 of Divatige Ramanahalli Village is Inam land.
28. It is say of D.W.1 that, he filed application/form before Land Tribunal seeking grant of property on the ground, he is in cultivation of same.
In further cross-examination of D.W.1 has deposed, Land Tribunal has not granted property to him.
Further it is deposed by defendant that, he has not filed any petition before Hon'ble High Court in this regard.

29. It is pertinent to note here that, once, land is Inam land as stated by defendant, it is clear that,
after coming into force of Karnataka Certain Inams Abolition Act, 1977 entire Sy.No.8 vest with Government.
If that is so, unless there is re-grant by competent authority either in favour of defendant or original owner Narayanappa, defendant cannot claim any right over said property.

Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
7 30.
The P.W.1 in his cross-examination has deposed, original owner Narayanappa is no more.
It is specifically deposed by D.W.1 that, he sought his title over suit property by way of adverse possession against Krishna Muniya, Smt. Chandramma and others.

31. It is to be noted here, by virtue of Ex.P.7 executed by Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society in favour of Nanjaiah, plaintiffs being legal heirs of said Nanjaiah have acquired title and possession over suit property.
It is not case of defendant that, he admitting either Nanjaiah or plaintiffs herein as owner of suit property set up his claim of adverse possession against these persons and succeeded in the same.

32. The learned counsel for defendant has argued that, in death certificate of Smt. Nanjamma as per Ex.P.60 and Aadhaar cards produced as per Exs.P.61 to P.63 suit schedule property address is not mentioned.

It is worth to note here that, as already discussed above, by virtue of possession certificate, Nanjaiah got possession of suit property from Binni Mills Housing Co-operative Society and there are other documents such as tax paid receipts and khata to show, plaintiffs are in possession and enjoyment of suit property.

33. When plaintiffs being owners of suit property acquired same under registered sale deed, they have produced revenue documents and other documents to show, their possession over suit property, it has to be accepted plaintiffs are in possession and enjoyment of suit property.
34. The defendant mainly based on documents pertaining to earlier proceedings and copy of complaints and photos cannot claim he is in possession and enjoyment of suit property.

Very claim of defendant that, he is in possession of suit property and constructed cattle shed in suit property and defendant also denying possession and enjoyment over suit property, it can safely concluded defendant is interfering in plaintiffs' possession and enjoyment of suit property.
Hence, I answer Issues No.1 and 2 in the affirmative.

35. ISSUES NO.3 AND 4 :- As these issues are inter-related to each other and involves common appreciation of facts and evidence on record, findings on one issue are bearing on other issue, in order to avoid repetition of facts and for convenience sake, both issues are taken together for common discussion.
36. According to defendant, plaintiffs are not in possession of suit property, as such suit for bare injunction itself is not maintainable.
Further it is contention of defendant that, he acquired suit property under relinquishment deed executed by Narayanappa as such suit of the plaintiff for bare injunction is not maintainable.

37. As already discussed, it is not case of defendant, Narayanappa having valid right and title over suit property even after coming into force of Karnataka Certain Inams Abolition Act, legally and validly under registered relinquishment deed relinquished his right and title over Sy.No.8 Divatige Ramanahalli Village in favour of defendant.

Per contra, ancestor of plaintiffs Nanjaiah had acquired title and possession over suit property by virtue registered sale deed as per Ex.P.7.
Nanjamma vs M Puttaswamy on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33376101/
8 38.
In view of above mentioned facts, it can safely held, defendant has not proved he has got better title over suit property than that of plaintiff.
Even in earlier proceedings filed by defendant against others, his right and title over suit property which is part of Sy.No.8 at Divatige Ramanahalli Village is not decided by court in his favour.
As such, suit filed by plaintiff for mere injunction against is maintainable.

39. It is required to be noted here, defendant mainly based on findings recorded by courts in earlier proceedings filed by him against some other persons cannot assert his lawful possession and enjoyment over suit property against plaintiffs, who are true owners of suit property based on Ex.P.7 and P.8.
40.

The plaintiffs having proved, their ancestor Nanjaiah got title and possession over suit property,
they are entitled for injunctive relief as prayed in plaint.

The defendant cannot claim his right or possession over suit property mainly based on earlier proceedings filed against legal heirs of Narayanappa and others, in which original plaintiff, Najaiah of present plaintiffs are not parties,
Hence, I answer Issue No.3 in the negative and issue No.4 in the affirmative.
41. ISSUES No.5 :- In view of the above said findings on Issue Nos. 1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby decreed with costs.

The defendant, his men, agents, servants or anybody claiming through him are hereby restrained by way of permanent injunction from interfering with plaintiffs'
possession and enjoyment of suit property.
Draw decree accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed & computerized by her,
corrected and signed by me and then pronounced in the open Court on this the 2nd day of February, 2026).

(BALAPPA APPANNA JARAGU) XXVIII Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge,
Mayohall, Bengaluru. ANNEXURE 1.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Husband of original plaintiff during his lifetime executed Will dated 01.12.2008 bequeathing suit property in favour of plaintiff.
Husband of plaintiff died on 09.12.2008.
By virtue of Will executed by her husband, original plaintiff become absolute owner and in possession and enjoyment of suit property.
On 02.12.2022,
plaintiff attempted to start construction of compound Wall to suit property, all of sudden defendant appeared and started to interfere in plaintiffs possession and enjoyment of suit property by contending he has filed suit in O.S.No.4334/2021 against Sri Deva Kumar, Rajesh and Mahadev.
Plaintiff is not party to O.S.No.4334/2021.
Defendant is stranger to plaintiff and suit property.
The defendant allegedly being care taker of one Narayanaswamy is claiming illegal right over alleged land left behind by Narayanaswamy.
There is no agricultural land near suit property.
The defendant who is not in physical possession or who having no right,
title and interest is attempting to take physical possession of suit property.
Plaintiff is not in possession of suit property.
Defendant was working with said Narayanappa in his Farm house constructed in Sy.No.8.
Narayanappa was cultivating said land by using Vrushabhavathi River Water and he was doing Horticulture and Animal husbandry with help of defendant.
Narayanappa settled in abroad in the year 1980 by executing letter of relinquishment of right and title dated 06.08.1980 in said property in the name of defendant and handed over physical possession of entire land bearing Sy.No.8 to defendant.
Thereafter, defendant has been continued in possession of entire Sy.No.8 including suit schedule property.
The defendant to the knowledge of true owner has continued in possession of above mentioned property for more than 40 years, hence he become absolute owner of suit property by virtue of adverse possession.
The defendant is residing in suit property and also running animal husbandry business.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. The original plaintiff has claimed her title and possession over suit schedule mentioned property based on registered Will dated 01.12.2008 said to have been executed by her husband Sri Nanjaiah in respect of suit property in her favour.
Registration of sale deed reinforces valid execution of sale deed and carries presumption of validity.
Burden of proof lies on party challenging validity.
It is for the other party challenging genuineness of transaction to show transaction is not valid in law.
A registered document therefore, prima facie would be valid in law.
If that is so, unless there is re-grant by competent authority either in favour of defendant or original owner Narayanappa, defendant cannot claim any right over said property.
33. When plaintiffs being owners of suit property acquired same under registered sale deed, they have produced revenue documents and other documents to show, their possession over suit property, it has to be accepted plaintiffs are in possession and enjoyment of suit property.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In this regard, the learned counsel for plaintiffs has relied upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in AIR 209 SC 72 in case of Jamila Begum (Dead) by LR's Vs. Shami Mohammed (d) by LR's wherein it is held that, a registered document carries with it a presumption that it was validly executed.
32. The learned counsel for defendant has argued that, in death certificate of Smt. Nanjamma as per Ex.P.60 and Aadhaar cards produced as per Exs.P.61 to P.63 suit schedule property address is not mentioned.
opennyai_summary.decision:
41. ISSUES No.5 :- In view of the above said findings on Issue Nos. 1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby decreed with costs.
The defendant, his men, agents, servants or anybody claiming through him are hereby restrained by way of permanent injunction from interfering with plaintiffs'
possession and enjoyment of suit property.
Draw decree accordingly.
